categoryNote: Monitoring/diagnostic-only category. Directive rule: NO universal fan-control registry tweaks and NO unsupported firmware modifications. Every entry here reads OS/vendor-exposed telemetry and states its source and limits; unavailable values are marked 'Uncertain-Unavailable' or 'Uncertain-VendorDependent' instead of fabricated numbers. NX10-008 writes exactly one log file to an owner-chosen path and changes no Windows configuration. No performance claim exists anywhere in this category. NX09 owns power-plan writes; NX03 owns processor power settings; NX10 only reads them.

tweaks.name: CPU temperature & throttling detection report
tweaks.description: Read-only report of CPU temperature from every OS-exposed source plus clock-frequency signals, with source attribution and explicit uncertainty; never asserts throttling.
tweaks.objective: Give the owner an honest picture of what Windows can and cannot report about CPU temperature, instead of a single fabricated number.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Get-NxCpuThermalReport queries three independent temperature sources and two clock signals. (1) Win32_TemperatureProbe (root\cimv2) is Microsoft-documented, and that documentation states current WMI implementations do NOT populate CurrentReading - so zero instances or zero readings are EXPECTED and are reported as Uncertain-Unavailable, never as 0 degrees. (2) MSAcpi_ThermalZoneTemperature (root\WMI) returns tenths of degrees Kelvin (verified live: 3232 = 323.2 K = 50.0 C); the class is widely present but no current Microsoft documentation page could be verified on 2026-11-23, so it is carried as E0 provenance and its zone names are treated as opaque (a zone is not guaranteed to be a CPU package sensor). (3) The '\Thermal Zone Information(*)\Temperature' performance counter reports Kelvin on this machine (E0 provenance; counter names are localized, so non-English Windows fails closed). Clock signals are Win32_Processor CurrentClockSpeed/MaxClockSpeed/LoadPercentage (documented; CurrentClockSpeed is SMBIOS-derived and frequently static) and the advisory '\Processor Information(_Total)\% of Maximum Frequency' counter. A headline temperature is published only when exactly one source responds or when the available sources agree within 5 C; otherwise the state is 'Uncertain-SourceDisagreement' and every value is listed side by side - never averaged. The throttle assessment is a SIGNAL statement: classifiedAsThrottle is always false, and the conclusion is 'NoSignalDetected', 'PossibleReducedFrequency-Uncertain' or 'Uncertain-Unavailable' with its basis. Reduced frequency is not diagnostic of thermal throttling because power management and firmware limits produce the same signal. No performance claim is made or implied.
tweaks.defaultState: No NEXTRIX CPU thermal report; temperature visibility depends on whatever the OEM firmware exposes.
tweaks.proposedState: A structured report: per-source readings with evidence level and limitation, per-source uncertainty, a headline that refuses to publish a disputed value, and a non-asserting throttle signal assessment.

verify.procedure: Report carries three temperature source records, each with source/evidence/limitation/state; headline.state is in the uncertainty vocabulary and headline.celsius is null whenever the state is not 'Available'; throttleAssessment.classifiedAsThrottle is false; noWritesPerformed is true.

sideEffects: Brief WMI queries and two performance-counter reads; no configuration is touched.
documentationSource: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/cimwin32prov/win32-temperatureprobe (documents that CurrentReading is not populated; fetched 2026-11-23)
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/cimwin32prov/win32-processor (CurrentClockSpeed/MaxClockSpeed/LoadPercentage; fetched 2026-11-23)
MSAcpi_ThermalZoneTemperature and the Thermal Zone Information counter: E0 provenance (verified live on this machine, no verified Microsoft documentation page)
docs/RESEARCH_RECONCILIATION.md adopt register #5 (uncertainty states: missing is not off, read failure is a sentinel)
research/sources/r4-synergy-ultraos.md (HagsDetection/WindowsVersionService uncertainty modeling)

tweaks.name: GPU temperature & throttling report
tweaks.description: Read-only GPU temperature and clocks-event report: NVIDIA through nvidia-smi (vendor-reported throttle reasons), AMD/Intel marked vendor-dependent, never a synthesized number.
tweaks.objective: Report what each GPU vendor actually exposes so thermal decisions rest on vendor telemetry rather than guesswork.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Get-NxGpuThermalReport enumerates Win32_VideoController adapters and maps vendors from PCI VEN_ ids ('10DE' NVIDIA, '1002' AMD, '8086' Intel). For NVIDIA adapters one nvidia-smi invocation queries temperature, current/max graphics clocks, power draw and limits, fan speed, utilization and the clocks-event reason flags (named columns plus the raw bitmask, decoded into the documented reason names with unknown bits reported as unknown). The full field profile degrades to 'index,name,temperature.gpu' when a driver rejects a field, and every [N/A] field is reported as Uncertain-Unavailable for that field only - observed live on a laptop RTX 3050 where power.limit is [N/A] while enforced.power.limit reports 60.00 W. Throttle classification is the VENDOR's own flag set (classifiedByNextrix = false): thermal slowdown, power cap, other reason, idle or none. Telemetry is attached to an adapter only when the nvidia-smi row count matches the NVIDIA adapter count; otherwise it is listed separately with a mapping note rather than mis-attributed. AMD ADL/Radeon Software and Intel IGCL are SDK/GUI surfaces with no vendor-documented WMI read contract used by NEXTRIX, so those adapters are 'Uncertain-VendorDependent'. No clocks, power or voltage setter is ever invoked (nvidia-smi -pl/-lgc/-lmc/-r are never called).
tweaks.defaultState: No NEXTRIX GPU thermal report; telemetry visible only in vendor tools.
tweaks.proposedState: Per-adapter records with temperature state/value, clocks, vendor-reported throttle reasons and an explicit limitation for each vendor that exposes nothing readable.

verify.procedure: Report lists every adapter with a temperatureState; NVIDIA adapters show a numeric temperature or an explicit [N/A] limitation; non-NVIDIA discrete/integrated adapters are 'Uncertain-VendorDependent'; nvidiaSmi block reports availability, degraded query state and any mapping note; noWritesPerformed is true.

sideEffects: Runs nvidia-smi with a bounded timeout (killed if the driver hangs); no configuration is touched.
documentationSource: https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvidia-smi/index.html (query fields, [N/A] semantics, Clocks Event Reasons; fetched 2026-11-23)
https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvml-api/index.html (NVML clocks-throttle reason enum names)
Win32_VideoController (documented CIM class; vendor mapping by PCI VEN_ id)
research/sources/r4-synergy-ultraos.md (GpuVendorClassification: PCI vendor id first, unknown is not treated as a real vendor)

tweaks.name: CPU power-limit monitoring
tweaks.description: Read-only CPU package power-limit report: hardware PL1/PL2 are not exposed by documented Windows interfaces, so they are marked vendor-dependent and the documented OS policy context is reported separately.
tweaks.objective: Stop owners from chasing a number Windows cannot reliably provide, and show the OS-level policy that IS visible.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Get-NxCpuPowerLimitReport deliberately reports no PL1/PL2 wattage. Intel package limits live in RAPL MSR 0x610 and AMD limits in SMU firmware; reading either requires a kernel-mode driver, which NEXTRIX does not install or ship. The report therefore carries state 'Uncertain-VendorDependent' for the limits, states the reason and names the owner action (read them in the platform vendor's own tuning utility where the vendor supports it). What it does publish is the documented OS policy context read with powercfg /query: Maximum processor state (PROCTHROTTLEMAX), Minimum processor state (PROCTHROTTLEMIN) and Processor performance boost mode (PERFBOOSTMODE), each with AC and DC indexes, explicitly labelled 'OS policy context - NOT a hardware power limit', because firmware may apply a lower hardware limit regardless. Ownership boundaries are respected: NX03 owns processor-setting writes, so this function only reads and never writes. Vendor tuning utilities are detected by service display name only (existence level) so the owner knows where to look; NEXTRIX never drives them. Locale honesty: powercfg output is parsed in its documented English form and fails closed into Uncertain-Unavailable.
tweaks.defaultState: No NEXTRIX power-limit report; PL1/PL2 visible only in vendor utilities where supported.
tweaks.proposedState: A report that marks hardware limits Uncertain-VendorDependent (no fabricated watts) and publishes AC/DC OS processor policy as clearly separated context.

verify.procedure: powerLimit.state is 'Uncertain-VendorDependent' with pl1Watts/pl2Watts null and a stated reason; osPolicyContext.kind names it as not a hardware power limit; each policy record state is Available/NotExposedOnActivePlan/Uncertain-Unavailable; noWritesPerformed is true.

sideEffects: Three read-only powercfg /query calls and a service enumeration.
documentationSource: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/customize/power-settings/configure-processor-power-management-options (processor power management policy; fetched 2026-11-23)
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/design/device-experiences/powercfg-command-line-options (/query documented)

tweaks.name: GPU power-limit monitoring
tweaks.description: Read-only GPU power draw and limit report: NVIDIA fields from nvidia-smi (each independently optional), other vendors marked vendor-dependent; power limits are never written.
tweaks.objective: Show which GPU power limits the driver actually exposes, without ever changing them.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Get-NxGpuPowerLimitReport reports power.draw, power.limit, power.default_limit, power.max_limit and enforced.power.limit per NVIDIA GPU from one bounded nvidia-smi query. Each field is independent because drivers legitimately return [N/A] for some of them: observed live on a laptop RTX 3050, power.limit is [N/A] while enforced.power.limit = 60.00 W, default_limit = 60.00 W and max_limit = 75.00 W - laptop firmware enforces limits instead of exposing a settable driver limit. Missing fields stay null with a field note; headroomToMaxWatts is only computed when both enforced and max limits are numeric, and it is an observation, not a recommendation. AMD and Intel adapters are 'Uncertain-VendorDependent' because their power telemetry is only reachable through vendor SDK/GUI surfaces with no vendor-documented WMI read contract. The function never sets a limit: nvidia-smi -pl and vendor tuning tools write hardware/firmware state and are out of scope for this category (powerLimitChangesPerformed = false).
tweaks.defaultState: No NEXTRIX GPU power report; limits visible only in vendor tools.
tweaks.proposedState: Per-GPU records of vendor-reported power draw and limits, with [N/A] fields marked unavailable and non-NVIDIA adapters marked vendor-dependent.

verify.procedure: Each NVIDIA GPU record reports numeric-or-null power fields (never a guessed value) with a state; adaptersWithoutTelemetry carries 'Uncertain-VendorDependent' for AMD/Intel; powerLimitChangesPerformed is false.

sideEffects: One bounded nvidia-smi query; no configuration or firmware is touched.
documentationSource: https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvidia-smi/index.html (Power Readings and query field aliases; fetched 2026-11-23)
TWEAK_CATALOGUE.md NX10 row (GPU power limits vendor-dependent; E0)

tweaks.name: Fan speed monitoring (where exposed)
tweaks.description: Read-only fan speed report from Win32_Fan (requested RPM) and nvidia-smi fan percentage, with explicit unavailability; NEXTRIX never controls a fan.
tweaks.objective: Report fan telemetry where the platform exposes it and state plainly when it does not - no fan-control feature is created.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Get-NxFanSpeedReport uses two documented sources and nothing else. Win32_Fan (root\cimv2) is Microsoft-documented, but DesiredSpeed is the CURRENTLY REQUESTED speed in revolutions per minute when VariableSpeed is true - not a measured tachometer value - and most consumer firmware does not populate the class at all, so zero instances is normal and is reported as 'Uncertain-Unavailable' with that explanation rather than as 0 RPM. nvidia-smi fan.speed reports the intended fan speed as a percentage of maximum noise tolerance and is frequently [N/A] on laptops whose fan is controlled by the platform (observed live). Reading nothing is prefered to inventing a number, so every fan record carries its state. fanControlPerformed and fanControlSupported are hard false: this category contains no fan-curve registry tweak, no OEM fan-interface call, no firmware write and no EC access - the directive explicitly forbids universal fan control.
tweaks.defaultState: No NEXTRIX fan report; fan telemetry visible only where firmware/OEM tools expose it.
tweaks.proposedState: Fan records with source, speed kind and state; an explicit statement that fan control is never performed.

verify.procedure: Every fan record has source/speedKind/state; an empty result yields state 'Uncertain-Unavailable' with the firmware explanation; fanControlPerformed and fanControlSupported are false; noWritesPerformed is true.

sideEffects: None beyond a read-only WMI query and one bounded nvidia-smi query.
documentationSource: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/cimwin32prov/win32-fan (DesiredSpeed is the requested RPM, VariableSpeed; fetched 2026-11-23)
https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/nvidia-smi/index.html (Fan Speed is percent of maximum noise tolerance; fetched 2026-11-23)
TWEAK_CATALOGUE.md NX10 directive (no universal fan-control tweaks)

tweaks.name: OEM fan/cooling profile detection
tweaks.description: Read-only detection of OEM cooling/fan management layers (namespaces, thermal/fan class names, utility services): profile state stays Unknown and no interface is invoked.
tweaks.objective: Tell the owner which OEM layer exists so cooling-profile changes stay an explicit OEM-tool decision.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Get-NxOemCoolingProfile probes the OEM management namespaces used by Dell Command | Monitor (root\dcim\sysman), Lenovo (root\Lenovo), HP (root\HP) and ASUS (root\ASUS), plus the utility service families of Dell/Lenovo/HP/ASUS/MSI/Gigabyte/Acer/Razer. In a namespace that EXISTS it enumerates class NAMES matching thermal/fan/cool and reports them - it never invokes a method, never writes a BIOS setting, never touches firmware and never drives the OEM utility, so oemInterfaceInvoked and firmwareWriteAttempted are hard false. Because no vendor-documented readable cooling-profile contract is implemented, every profileState is 'Unknown' with an explicit uncertainty note; switchingSupport is 'None-NotImplemented'. Provenance is E0: the namespaces/services are community-known and per-OEM vendor documentation exists but was not fetched for this entry, so no state value is claimed. This deliberately mirrors the reference projects' decision to ship GPU/OEM materials as manual links rather than automated detection (r1, r4) and leaves any future switching to a per-OEM module with a vendor-documented interface.
tweaks.defaultState: No NEXTRIX OEM cooling report; cooling profile managed invisibly by the OEM utility.
tweaks.proposedState: A detection report: which OEM management layers and thermal/fan classes exist, with profile state Unknown and no writes.

verify.procedure: Every OEM record reports namespacesProbed, namespacesPresent, thermalFanClasses, matchingServices, profileState 'Unknown', methodInvocation 'none'; oemInterfaceInvoked and firmwareWriteAttempted are false; detectedCount matches the records flagged interfaceDetected.

sideEffects: Namespace class enumeration on OEM management namespaces that exist; service enumeration.
documentationSource: research/sources/r1-fsosx-xos.md (vendor GPU/OEM materials shipped as manual links, not automated detection; hardware logic gated on detection)
research/sources/r4-synergy-ultraos.md (GPU-vendor materials manual only; features gated on detected hardware)
TWEAK_CATALOGUE.md NX10-006 (only where an OEM documents an interface; per-OEM module; E0)

tweaks.name: AC/DC thermal behavior report
tweaks.description: Read-only AC/DC report: power source, active plan, processor policy planes and system cooling policy, with a documented statement that a real comparison needs observation on both sources.
tweaks.objective: Show the laptop AC/DC thermal-policy pairing Windows exposes, and route true comparison to the session logger instead of faking it from one snapshot.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Get-NxAcDcThermalReport reads the current power source (Win32_Battery BatteryStatus, corroborated by root\WMI BatteryStatus.PowerOnline where present) and, for the active plan, the AC and DC indexes of Maximum processor state, Minimum processor state, Processor performance boost mode and System cooling policy (SYSCOOLPOL) via READ-ONLY powercfg /query. Friendly names are taken from the plan's own 'Possible Setting Friendly Name' output, never from a hardcoded guess, so an enumerated setting such as cooling policy is translated only by what the plan itself reports. A documented setting that OEM images hide (SYSCOOLPOL is absent from the active plan on the authoring machine) is reported as 'NotExposedOnActivePlan' - a known absence, not uncertainty - while an unparseable query becomes 'Uncertain-Unavailable'. dcApplicable follows real battery presence, so desktops are not given a meaningless DC column. The report states in samplingNote that an AC-versus-DC thermal comparison requires observing the machine on both sources and points at NX10-008; taking one snapshot cannot produce a comparison. Nothing is written: NX09 owns power-plan writes and NX03 owns processor settings, and no registry value is touched.
tweaks.proposedState: A report with current power source and per-plane AC/DC indexes (or NotExposedOnActivePlan / Uncertain-Unavailable), plus guidance to use NX10-008 for a real comparison.

verify.procedure: powerSource.current is AC/Battery/Uncertain-Unavailable; each thermalPolicy plane state is Available/NotExposedOnActivePlan/Uncertain-Unavailable; dcApplicable equals hasBattery; samplingNote points at NX10-008; noWritesPerformed is true.

sideEffects: Five read-only powercfg calls plus WMI reads.
documentationSource: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/design/device-experiences/powercfg-command-line-options (/query, /getactivescheme documented)
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/customize/power-settings/configure-processor-power-management-options (processor power policy; fetched 2026-11-23)
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.windows.eventtracing.power.iprocessorperformanceconfiguration.systemcoolingpolicy (system cooling policy = active/passive; fetched 2026-11-23)
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/cimwin32prov/win32-battery (BatteryStatus semantics; fetched 2026-11-23)

tweaks.name: Thermal session logging for owner testing
tweaks.description: Bounded, read-only thermal sampling session that appends CSV rows to an owner-chosen log file; no Windows configuration is changed and the run is journaled.
tweaks.objective: Give the owner a reproducible evidence file for their own thermal testing (before/after, AC vs DC, game/benchmark runs) without changing anything on the machine.
tweaks.technicalExplanation: Invoke-NxThermalSessionLog samples the OS-exposed thermal/clock/power-source signals and NVIDIA telemetry at a fixed interval for a bounded duration (-DurationSeconds 1..3600, default 300; -SampleIntervalSeconds 1..300, default 10) and writes one CSV row per sample. The file starts with two '#' provenance comment lines (sources and their limits) followed by a stable header; a sample publishes a CPU temperature only when the available temperature sources agree within 5 C, otherwise it records 'Uncertain-SourceDisagreement' with both sources named. The path is MANDATORY: the function refuses placeholder text ('<user-chosen log file path>' is rejected with an explanation), creates only the chosen parent directory when missing, defaults the extension to .csv, and refuses to overwrite an existing file without -Append so the owner's evidence cannot be destroyed silently. Nothing in Windows is configured - no registry value, service, task, power setting, OEM interface or firmware - and changedConfiguration is always false. The journal record is deliberately a single 'verify' entry (result Success/Failed, targetType 'thermalSessionLog', changedConfiguration false) rather than an 'apply' entry: the rollback engine only considers 'apply' entries, and nothing here is restorable configuration. Privacy: the journal stores the log file's leaf name only (a full path can contain a user name) and no host name, user name, SID or serial is written to the log or the journal.
tweaks.proposedState: A CSV evidence file at the owner-chosen path, journaled as a diagnostic run with no configuration change.

verify.procedure: The chosen file exists with the provenance comment, header and >=1 data row; result reports sampleRows, bytes, changedConfiguration=false and journaled=true; the journal holds one 'verify' entry for NX10-008 with pathRecorded 'fileNameOnly'; a second run without -Append is refused.

rollback.procedure: Not applicable - no configuration changed; the log file is the owner's evidence and stays until the owner deletes it (append-only by design, never overwritten silently).

originalState.method: Not applicable - the run records whether the file existed before; nothing restorable changes.

sideEffects: Writes one CSV file at the owner-chosen path; sampling keeps the process busy for the chosen duration (default 300 s) with per-sample WMI/counter/nvidia-smi reads.
